title: Development of an Isothermal Assay for the Detection of Enteric Human Adenoviruses in Fresh Produce
content: The increased consumption of fresh produce has led to a rise in foodborne outbreaks caused by enteric viruses, which feature low infectious doses and high environmental persistence. Human adenovirus (HAdV) serves as a reliable indicator of this fecal con-tamination. To address this, a study developed a recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) assay to detect HAdV in 150 fresh produce samples sourced from wet markets, malls, and farms. The results showed 81 positive samples via quantitative PCR (qPCR) and 72 via RPA, with contamination highly prevalent in malls and wet markets, likely due to handling and transit. The RPA assay proved highly efficient, operating under isother-mal conditions of 35ºC for 40 minutes, thereby eliminating the need for complex thermal cyclers. It demonstrated strong statistical agreement with qPCR, achieving 90.28% sensi-tivity, 79.49% specificity, and 84.67% accuracy relative to qPCR as the reference method. With its simple operation and high efficiency, the developed RPA assay is a reliable screening method that serves as a promising alternative to qPCR for detecting HAdV in fresh produce, although further development is needed before it can be considered a true point-of-care test.
